slides.teacher_cue: New sound — qu. In English, q always comes before u and they always work as a team — /kw/. Start with the k sound at the back of the throat, then immediately round the lips for /w/. qu! qu! quick! quest! Important rule: q and u are always together in English — q is never used alone.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /kw/ cleanly and understand that qu is always a unit — q never appears without u.
slides.correction_move: Model qu as a rapid k-w blend. Students copy. Establish the rule: q and u are always together.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students trying to say just /k/ without the /w/ element.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the new focus, then connect qu to one strong word from today.
slides.expected_response: Students say qu clearly and connect it to a lesson word.
slides.correction_move: Model the focus once, then have students echo and use it in a known word.
slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say quick — fast. Confirm /kw/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say quick orally and connect meaning before blending on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model quick orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the /kw/ onset — both elements must be present.

slides.teacher_cue: Say quit — to stop. Confirm /kw/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say quit orally and connect meaning before blending on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model quit orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the /kw/ onset and clean final /t/.

slides.teacher_cue: Say quest — a long difficult search. Confirm /kw/ onset. Reveal print and blend all five sounds.
slides.expected_response: Students say quest orally and connect meaning before blending on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model quest orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /kw/ onset and the final st cluster.

slides.teacher_cue: Say quill — a feather used as a pen; also a spine of a porcupine. Confirm /kw/ onset. Blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say quill orally and connect meaning before blending on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model quill orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /kw/ onset, short /ɪ/, and /l/ in coda — /l/ vs /r/ check still active.
